facts.text: Severe allergic reactions (rash, facial swelling, asthma, hives, skin reddening, shock, blisters) may occur, especially in individuals allergic to aspirin. Stop use and seek medical help immediately if symptoms appear.
facts.population: All patients, heightened risk in aspirin‑allergic individuals

facts.text: Ibuprofen (an NSAID) can cause serious stomach bleeding. Risk is increased with higher/longer dosing, concurrent anticoagulant or steroid use, history of ulcers or bleeding, ≥3 alcoholic drinks per day, age ≥ 60, or use of other NSAIDs.
facts.population: All patients; higher risk in elderly and those with GI risk factors

facts.text: NSAIDs (except aspirin) raise the risk of heart attack, heart failure, and stroke; risk rises with higher or prolonged use. Do not use if you have had a prior allergic reaction to any pain/fever reducer or if you are peri‑operative for heart surgery.
facts.population: All patients; especially those with cardiovascular disease

facts.text: Ibuprofen may diminish the cardioprotective effect of low‑dose aspirin taken for heart attack or stroke prevention.
facts.population: Patients taking low‑dose aspirin for cardiovascular protection

facts.text: Concurrent use of other prescription or non‑prescription NSAIDs (e.g., aspirin, naproxen) increases risk of GI bleeding and cardiovascular events.
Patients aged 60 years or older have an increased risk of stomach bleeding and should use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration possible.
Patients with pre‑existing kidney disease are at higher risk for renal adverse effects; monitor renal function and avoid excessive dosing.

Adults and children ≥ 12 years: 1 tablet every 4–6 hours as needed; if pain/fever persists, a second tablet may be taken. Do not exceed 6 tablets in 24 hours unless directed by a physician. Children < 12 years: consult a doctor before use.
